# Gyan Kumar Sah

> Physics student at SRM University-AP who builds lab instruments and the software that runs them. Looking for a six-month research internship in quantum hardware, January to June 2027, and later a PhD in quantum hardware. This file describes his work in plain words; technical details follow each item.

## Research and lab work (SRM University-AP)

- Temperature control for the lab's probe station (2026, Low Temperature Physics Lab, with Dr. Krishna Prasad Maity). The vacuum chamber used for measurements kept overshooting its target temperature. He found the controller setting that caused it and wrote the software that now runs the measurements unattended. Details: Janis ST-LN-500 probe station, Cryo-con 22C controller, Wayne Kerr impedance analyser; overshoot reduced from +4.08 K to +0.22 K over 297 to 450 K; works from 300 to 450 K at 10^-2 mbar (liquid-nitrogen cooling is planned, not running); automated impedance spectroscopy from 20 Hz to 10 MHz; an isolated relay cutoff at 470 K. Code: https://github.com/sahgyan9/Cryocon_22C_Temperature_Controller_Python-File
- A light sensor from cadmium selenide and graphene quantum dots (CdSe:GQD photodetector; 2025 to 2026, Device Physics Lab; with Akshay Sampath and Nilja George, under Dr. Maity). Mixing the two materials made the sensor respond about ten times faster (rise time 200 ms to 20 ms). He built and automated the measurement setup. Details: responsivity 0.098 A/W, specific detectivity 1.5 x 10^11 Jones. A draft paper exists; it has not been submitted.
- Magnetic field and photocurrent in chromium-doped CdSe (Jan to Apr 2026, Device Physics Lab, with Visitha Padilam), funded by the university's UG/PG SEED Grant. Data collected; no report yet.
- PMN-PT dielectric study (Sep 2026, Device Physics Lab): how a ceramic stores charge from 300 to 460 K, measured with his automated setup.
- MoS2 thin film (Sep to Nov 2026): XRD, XPS and UV spectroscopy reports on a film grown by chemical vapour deposition.
- Electrospun PVDF, PVA and PVA-Ag nanofibres (Aug to Nov 2026, course project with Dr. Pranab Mandal). Fibres of about 100 to 130 nm. No silver was detected in the PVA-Ag sample.
- Cobalt thin film (2025, Exotic Interface Lab): a 30 nm sputtered cobalt Hall bar. The anomalous Hall measurement was attempted, gave no usable data, and the work was discontinued.
- Quantum Reference Center, SRM University-AP (2026): a small supporting role, helping with system integration (vacuum, cryogenics, electronics) while the centre is set up.

## Work

- Production Engineer, Shakti Photon Solutions Pvt. Ltd. (Feb 2025 to present). A startup on the SRM AP campus that builds hydrogen electrolysers and fuel cells. He fabricates membrane electrode assemblies, machines parts (Fusion 360, CNC, 3D printing), writes lab procedures, worked on the design of a 30 x 30 cm electrolyser, built a hydrogen leak detector, commissioned a fuel-cell balance-of-plant system at IIT Delhi, and wrote a Python program for electrochemical tests on an ITECH power supply (https://github.com/sahgyan9/IT-M39002C-PowerSupply). He also built the company website (https://shakti-photon-solutions.vercel.app).

## Leadership

- Track Lead, Technical and Innovation Track, Qiskit Fall Fest 2026, SRM University-AP (Sep to Oct 2026; https://www.qffsrmap2026.com). A student-run quantum computing festival. He led three cells through their heads: Technical Programs (Baratam Praneeth Gupta), Hackathon and Competition (Sri Vastava Sri Harsha Gampa) and Website and Technology (Srihaas Pigilam). The Quantum Capture the Flag contest was built and run by Jaswanth Kumar Kondameeda; Gyan supervised. Offline games were run by Jyoshna Pilli and her team. Gyan wrote a large part of the festival platform (a team product), built the tool that scored the hackathon's first round, and taught the hands-on Qiskit session. Hackathon finale: 45 teams confirmed, 44 present, 196 members.
- Led the Aadigyan Winter Youth Program (IR Council, SRM University-AP, 2024), which hosted students and teachers from Nepal.

## Projects

- Superconducting qubit designs in Keysight ADS (Aug 2026). Designed and simulated, not fabricated: a single transmon with a readout resonator, and two transmons with a bus coupler, exported to GDSII.
- Oberleaf (Sep 2026 to present, solo, MIT licence): a free LaTeX editor that compiles on the user's own computer and explains errors in plain English. https://github.com/sahgyan9/Oberleaf
- Friendly Learning SRMAP (Dec 2024 to present, founder, mostly solo): a campus website for finding mentors and looking up faculty research. Still small: 27 registered accounts and 4 verified mentors. https://friendly-learning-srmap.vercel.app
- Quantum Ascent (Jul to Aug 2026, solo): a free six-step course from a single qubit to the QAOA algorithm, with a simulator in the browser. https://quantum-ascent-77617.web.app
- NEPSE Portfolio Insight (Jul to Nov 2026, solo): a private portfolio tracker for Nepal Stock Exchange investors. He pre-registered a test of its stock-ranking score; the score did not beat a matched benchmark, and he reports it that way. https://github.com/sahgyan9/NEPSE-Portfolio-Insight
- Quantum Double Shield Protocol (Aug 2025, team): BB84 key distribution with a quantum random number generator in Qiskit. Third place, Amaravati Quantum Valley Hackathon. https://qdsp.lovable.app/
- Nepali Village Calculator (2026): a loan-interest calculator in Nepali and English using Bikram Sambat dates. https://village-calculator.vercel.app
- Email-to-calendar helper (May 2026): Google Apps Script with the Mistral API.

## How he thinks

- Believe in the power of compounding: in learning, relationships and investing.
- Think from fundamentals, and build things by hand to understand them.
- A tool should explain itself (human-centred design, after Don Norman).
- Build what does not exist yet.
- Give credit by name.
- Long term: build a business that funds scientists, and bring quantum technology to Nepal.
